opening: The gut microbiome is a critical regulator of systemic immunity and a major modulator of response to cancer immunotherapy with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). However, the clinical implementation of microbiome-inspired therapies that leverage these associations have proven challenging. Probiotics—live microorganisms thought to confer health benefits as part of food or food supplements—have gained increasing attention as readily testable, low-toxicity agents with potential of favorably influencing host–microbiome–immune interactions in the context of cancer immunotherapy. ents with potential of favorably influencing host–microbiome–immune interactions in the context of cancer immunotherapy.
